replayDesignReview.reasonExplicitContractIsNecessary: Original fetch requires same-run artifact ownership and a successful producer in that run. Original context compares current run/attempt/head/fixture plus all nonhistoric environment fields. Blind cross-run reuse would introduce a provenance/context rejection different from the now-identified checkpoint-link-mismatch stopping guard.
requirements: Keep the default same-run fetch and complete context equality behavior unchanged when explicit replay opt-in is absent.

Bind a fixed immutable origin lock to run39197008470, headfdc6722b6ac5467f7baf6c0fa6a3537ee0a51860, fixture4337d51a228834f4b2cbee1f4ef0771eb45737a8, successful producer117881829274, artifact12164479528, exact bytes/archive+manifest digests, expiry and producer build date.
Verify actual current run/head/attempt/current job through real environment and ordinary API independently of origin. Do not overwrite GITHUB metadata.

Verify the original completed run, attempt1 and exact locked head; require the exact original producer job completed successfully and the sole unexpired artifact's run, name, size, digest and retention. The original run's overall failure is compatible with a successful producer and must not be represented as run success.

Require identical complete context key sets. Compare only the four declared historical run/attempt/head/fixture keys against locked origin; compare every other field and nested roots against actual current context without silently dropping unknown fields.
Keep plan SHA, absolute canonical roots, runtime/harness/repository/image/Python SHA, source/reference content/modes, all payload hashes/links/mtime and trusted completion checks unchanged.

Bind producer build date and retain both origin and current execution receipts. Do not modify the archive or its manifest/context to make a mismatch disappear.
